arxiv-1706-05037.title: Model based approach to study Defect Dependency in Large Scale Integrated Software Products
arxiv-1706-05037.creator: Sai Anirudh Karre Y. Raghu Reddy
arxiv-1706-05037.description: Abstract Large organizations have diverse product offerings to meet various business needs. To increase revenue, its common these days to offer software products as integrated product suite(s) rather than individual products. Creating and maintaining high quality software products within the integrated product suite requires rigorous product engineering methods.

arxiv-1708-00137.title: Causation does not explain contextuality
arxiv-1708-00137.creator: Sally Shrapnel, Fabio Costa
arxiv-1708-00137.description: Abstract Realist interpretations of quantum mechanics presuppose the existence of elements of reality that are independent of the actions used to reveal them. Such a view is challenged by several no-go theorems that show quantum correlations cannot be explained by non-contextual ontological models, where physical properties are assumed to exist prior to and independently of the act of measurement.

arxiv-2101-02713.title: Measuring the primordial gravitational wave background in the presence of other stochastic signals
arxiv-2101-02713.creator: D. Poletti
arxiv-2101-02713.description: Abstract Standard methodologies for the extraction of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) from auto- or cross-correlation of interferometric signals often involve the use of a filter function. The standard optimal filter maximizes the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) between the total SGWB and the noise.

arxiv-2201-07094.description: Abstract . We define fractional derivatives ∂ t α \partial_{t}^{\alpha} in Sobolev spaces based on L p ​ ( 0 , T ) L^{p}(0,T) by an operator theory, and characterize the domain of ∂ t α \partial_{t}^{\alpha} in subspaces of the Sobolev-Slobodecki spaces W α , p ​ ( 0 , T ) W^{\alpha,p}(0,T) .

arxiv-2201-11220.title: DiGamma: Domain-aware Genetic Algorithm for HW-Mapping Co-optimization for DNN Accelerators Thanks: This work was supported by NSF Award 1909900. This work is available at https://github.com/maestro-project/digamma.
arxiv-2201-11220.creator: Sheng-Chun Kao 1 , Michael Pellauer 2 , Angshuman Parashar 2 , Tushar Krishna 1
arxiv-2201-11220.description: Abstract The design of DNN accelerators includes two key parts: HW resource configuration and mapping strategy. Intensive research has been conducted to optimize each of them independently. Unfortunately, optimizing for both together is extremely challenging due to the extremely large cross-coupled search space.

arxiv-2211-04265.title: Photon shot-noise limited transient absorption soft X-ray spectroscopy at the European XFEL
arxiv-2211-04265.creator: Andrea, Martin, William, Florian, Cammille, David, Naman, Christine, Uwe, Jens, Robert, Andrea, Alessandro, Jan-Torben, Wajid, Robin, Florian, Hans, Peter, Carlo, Alexander, Luca, Michael, Natalia, Rafael, Karsten, Steffen, Manuel, Emmanuelle, Ebad, Suren, Thomas, Tim, Tobias, David, Stefano, Talgat
arxiv-2211-04265.description: Abstract Femtosecond transient soft X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) is a very promising technique that can be employed at X-ray Free Electron Lasers (FELs) to investigate out-of-equilibrium dynamics for material and energy research. Here we present a dedicated setup for soft X-rays available at the Spectroscopy & Coherent Scattering (SCS) instrument at the European X-ray Free Electron Laser (EuXFEL).

arxiv-2309-00704.title: Nowhere-zero 8-flows in cyclically 5-edge-connected, flow-admissible signed graphs
arxiv-2309-00704.creator: Matt DeVos Kathryn Nurse Robert Šámal, Matt DeVos, Kathryn Nurse, Robert Šámal
arxiv-2309-00704.description: Abstract In 1983, Bouchet proved that every bidirected graph with a nowhere-zero integer-flow has a nowhere-zero 216-flow, and conjectured that 216 could be replaced with 6. This paper shows that for cyclically 5-edge-connected bidirected graphs that number can be replaced with 8. 1 Introduction A signed graph consists of a graph G together with a signature \sigma:E(G)\rightarrow\{-1,1\} .

arxiv-2311-13369.title: Note on Disjoint Cycles in Multipartite Tournaments
arxiv-2311-13369.creator: Gregory Gutin, Wei Li, Shujing Wang, Anders Yeo, Yacong Zhou
arxiv-2311-13369.description: Abstract In 1981, Bermond and Thomassen conjectured that for any positive integer k k , every digraph with minimum out-degree at least 2 ​ k − 1 2k-1 admits k k vertex-disjoint directed cycles. In this short paper, we verify the Bermond-Thomassen conjecture for triangle-free multipartite tournaments and 3-partite tournaments.

arxiv-2402-10349.title: Ultrafast electron diffraction of photoexcited gas-phase cyclobutanone predicted by ab initio multiple cloning simulations
arxiv-2402-10349.creator: Dmitry V. Makhov, Adam Kirrander, Dmitrii V. Shalashilin
arxiv-2402-10349.description: Abstract We present the result of our calculations of ultrafast electron diffraction (UED) for cyclobutanone excited into S 2 S_{2} electronic state, which are based on the non-adiabatic dynamics simulations with Ab Initio Multiple Cloning (AIMC) method with the electronic structure calculated at the SA(3)-CASSCF(12,12)/aug-cc-pVDZ level of theory.

arxiv-2405-19334.title: LLMs Meet Multimodal Generation and Editing: A Survey Thanks: † Project leaders; * Co-first authors. Yingqing He, Zhaoyang Liu, Jingye Chen, Zeyue Tian, Hongyu Liu, Xiaowei Chi, Runtao Liu, Ruibin Yuan, Yazhou Xing, Wei Xue, Qifeng Liu, Yike Guo, and Qifeng Chen are with The Hong Kong University of
arxiv-2405-19334.creator: Yingqing He † *, Zhaoyang Liu † *, Jingye Chen *, Zeyue Tian *, Hongyu Liu *, Xiaowei Chi *
arxiv-2405-19334.description: Abstract With the recent advancement in large language models (LLMs), there is a growing interest in combining LLMs with multimodal learning. Previous surveys of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) mainly focus on multimodal understanding . This survey elaborates on multimodal generation and editing across various domains, comprising image, video, 3D, and audio.

arxiv-2506-17518.title: A Survey of State Representation Learning for Deep Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2506-17518.creator: Ayoub Echchahed ayoub.echchahed@mila.quebec, Pablo Samuel Castro psc@google.com
arxiv-2506-17518.description: Abstract Representation learning methods are an important tool for addressing the challenges posed by complex observations spaces in sequential decision making problems. Recently, many methods have used a wide variety of types of approaches for learning meaningful state representations in reinforcement learning, allowing better sample efficiency, generalization, and performance.

arxiv-2507-09743.title: How homogeneous was the chemical enrichment of the Milky Way 13 gigayears ago?
arxiv-2507-09743.creator: Riano E. Giribaldi 1, Laura Magrini 1, Martina Rossi 2,3, Anish Amarsi 4, Davide Massari 3, Donatela Romano 3
arxiv-2507-09743.description: Abstract We reanalyze the chemical composition of the metal-poorest tail of the Galactic halo using highly accurate atmospheric parameters ( Giribaldi et. al 2021 ; Giribaldi et. al 2023 ) and cutting-edge 3D NLTE models ( Amarsi et. al 2018 ) .

arxiv-2508-13387.title: SPANER: Shared Prompt Aligner for Multimodal Semantic Representation
arxiv-2508-13387.creator: Thye Shan Ng, Soyeon Caren Han, Eun-Jung Holden
arxiv-2508-13387.description: Abstract Recent advances in multimodal Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) have significantly improved performance on downstream tasks such as few-shot retrieval. However, most existing approaches focus on task-specific gains while neglecting the structure of the multimodal embedding space. As a result, modality-specific representations often remain isolated, limiting cross-modal generalisation.

arxiv-2508-14113.title: Federated Action Recognition for Smart Worker Assistance Using FastPose Thanks: This work was funded by the Carl Zeiss Stiftung, Germany under the Sustainable Embedded AI project (P2021-02-009).
arxiv-2508-14113.creator: Vinit Hegiste, Vidit Goyal, Tatjana Legler, Martin Ruskowski
arxiv-2508-14113.description: Abstract In smart manufacturing environments, accurate and real-time recognition of worker actions is essential for productivity, safety, and human–machine collaboration. While skeleton-based human activity recognition (HAR) offers robustness to lighting, viewpoint, and background variations, most existing approaches rely on centralized datasets, which are impractical in privacy-sensitive industrial scenarios.

arxiv-2509-21620.title: Dirac QNM spectrum from twisted semiclassical gauge theory of gravity
arxiv-2509-21620.creator: Marija Dimitrijević Ćirić 1, Nikola Herceg 2, Nikola Konjik 3, A. Naveena Kumara 4 and Andjelo Samsarov 5
arxiv-2509-21620.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marija Dimitrijević Ćirić 1, Nikola Herceg 2, Nikola Konjik 3, A. Naveena Kumara 4 and Andjelo Samsarov 5. Twisted Abelian gauge theory coupled to a noncommutative (NC) Dirac field is studied in order to infer the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum of the fermion matter perturbations in the vicinity of the Reissner-Nordström (RN) black hole. The action functional of the theory is invariant under the truncated NC local U ​ ( 1 ) ⋆ U(1)_{\star} gauge transformations that keep the gravitational background intact.

arxiv-2512-02182.title: Efficient and Intuitive Two-Phase Validation Across Multiple Models via Principal Components
arxiv-2512-02182.creator: Sarah C. Lotspeich, Cole Manschot
arxiv-2512-02182.description: Abstract Two-phase sampling offers a cost-effective way to validate error-prone measurements in observational databases or randomized trials. Inexpensive or easy-to-obtain information is collected for the entire study in Phase I. Then, a subset of patients undergoes cost-intensive validation to collect more accurate data in Phase II.

arxiv-2512-08016.title: FRIEDA : Benchmarking Multi-Step Cartographic Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2512-08016.creator: Jiyoon Pyo Yuankun Jiao Dongwon Jung Zekun Li, Leeje Jang Sofia Kirsanova Jina Kim Yijun Lin Qin Liu Junyi Xie, Hadi Askari Nan Xu Muhao Chen Yao-Yi Chiang
arxiv-2512-08016.description: Abstract Cartographic reasoning is the skill of interpreting geographic relationships by aligning legends, map scales, compass directions, map texts, and geometries across one or more map images. Although essential as a concrete cognitive capability and for critical tasks such as disaster response and urban planning, it remains largely unevaluated.

arxiv-2604-03657.creator: Tianci Luo, Haohao Pan, Jinpeng Wang, Niu Lian, Xinrui Chen, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia, Chun Yuan

arxiv-2606-03552.creator: Yu-Jie Huang, Wei Dai, Jiaxing Zhao, Tan Luo, Ben-Wei Zhang, Enke Wang

europmc-pmc7737089.creator: Madewell ZJ, Yang Y, Longini IM, Halloran ME, Dean NE.
europmc-pmc7737089.description: Importance Crowded indoor environments, such as households, are high-risk settings for the transmission of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Objectives To examine evidence for household transmission of SARS-CoV-2, disaggregated by several covariates,

pmc-10595682.title: Time to act! A review exploring the impact of climate change on respiratory diseases
pmc-10595682.creator: K Scerri, S Cuschieri
pmc-10595682.description: BackgroundClimate change is a growing global epidemic, with negative repercussions on various determinants including an impact on non-communicable diseases. Respiratory diseases contribute to a substantial global burden. Therefore, exploring the relationships and impact between the growing climate change epidemic and respiratory diseases are of utmost clinical importance.

pmc-10597110.title: Outbreak economic analysis of six imported hemorrhagic fevers following detection at 24 hours
pmc-10597110.creator: T Learoyd, K Yeo
pmc-10597110.description: A ten-language search found no economic analysis of symptomatic hemorrhagic fever importation for Crimean Congo (CCHF), Hantavirus (HV), Lassa (LV), Marburg (MARV), Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) or Nipah (NV) into the USA/EU/UK. This study used available literature to calculate the cost of importation of the six selected fevers with each outbreak detected at 24 hours.

pmc-11639781.title: Circulating Hepcidin Levels Are an Independent Predictor of Survival in Microsatellite Stable Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patient Candidates for Standard First-Line Treatment
pmc-11639781.creator: Vincenzo Formica, Antonio Di Grazia, Maria Vittoria Bonomo, Rachele Frascatani, Roberto Mancone, Giovanni Monteleone
pmc-11639781.description: Simple SummaryHepcidin, a peptide hormone, is overexpressed in colorectal cancer, mainly in the advanced stages. This study assessed whether the pre-treatment serum levels of hepcidin are a predictive factor of the overall survival of patients with microsatellite stable metastatic colorectal cancer receiving first-line treatment with FOLFOX-panitumumab (RAS/BRAF wild-type) or FOLFOX-bevacizumab (RAS or BRAF mutations).

pmc-12243985.title: Depression and anxiety outcomes of adults undergoing intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) treatment for major depressive disorder: A naturalistic study
pmc-12243985.creator: Noah A Lee, Simon Kung, Yuliang Hu, Stacy E Greenwaldt, Maria I Lapid, Paul E Croarkin
pmc-12243985.description: BackgroundStandard repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) are approved treatments for major depressive disorder (MDD). iTBS offers shorter treatment durations and increased accessibility. This study examines the clinical outcomes of iTBS for MDD in a tertiary medical center.MethodsPatients who underwent iTBS for MDD at Mayo Clinic Rochester between March 2021 and January 2023 were included.

pmc-12406650.title: Are respiratory risks after cardiac surgery universal? A case study from Tuzla, Bosnia and Herzegovina
pmc-12406650.creator: Alisa Krdžalić, Amar Skakić, Omar Krdžalić, Ivana Iveljić
pmc-12406650.description: ObjectivePostoperative respiratory complications (PRCs) are a significant concern after cardiac surgery, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to analyze the incidence and risk factors for PRCs in a tertiary center in Bosnia and Herzegovina and compare findings with data from developed countries.

pmc-12836778.title: Comparing the digital dynamometer and Martin vigorimeter for handgrip strength: reliability, agreement, and prognostic value
pmc-12836778.creator: Shuyue Luo, Xiaoyan Chen, Rongna Lian, Huiyu Tang, Zecong Chen, Wenhua Jiang, Jiaojiao Jiang, Ming Yang
pmc-12836778.description: BackgroundHandgrip strength (HGS) measurement is vital for clinical assessment in older adults, yet comparative performance of different devices in Asian populations remains understudied. Prior validation focused mainly on healthy adults, but this is the first comprehensive comparison in institutionalized older adults with cognitive impairment and ADL disability.

pmc-13024264.title: The Extracellular Matrix in Liver Regeneration: Biological and Therapeutic Insights
pmc-13024264.creator: Haodong Ma, Wenyue Wu, Wen Zhang, Hong Li, Ziyan Pan, Caihong Wang, Ruoyu Gao, Qiushuang Ji, Zhi Chen, Hong You, Wei Chen
pmc-13024264.description: The liver possesses a remarkable regenerative capacity following injury, a process fundamentally orchestrated by the dynamic extracellular matrix (ECM). Far beyond a passive scaffold, the liver matrisome functions as an integrative mechano-biochemical circuit. It comprises a core structural network together with regulatory non-core components that collectively establish a dynamic niche.

pmc-13153463.title: Redescription and embryonic developmental dynamics of Aphelenchoides bicaudatus with implications for nematode taxonomy and ecology
pmc-13153463.creator: Min Li, Ying Pei, Yanmei Shi, Fengmao Chen, Lifeng Zhou
pmc-13153463.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryAphelenchoides bicaudatus is widely reported yet frequently confused with morphologically similar congeners. bicaudatus recovered from declining Pinus massoniana and associated Monochamus alternatus in eastern China using integrated light microscopy, SEM, and rDNA markers (ITS and SSU). Key diagnostic characters, particularly the bifurcated female tail terminus and SEM-resolved lip annulation, matched prior descriptions and were supported by congruent maximum-likelihood phylogenetic placement with reference sequences.

pmc-13562948.title: The genome sequence of the Pale Eggar, Trichiura crataegi (Linnaeus, 1758) (Lepidoptera: Lasiocampidae)
pmc-13562948.creator: Owen T. Lewis, Liam M. Crowley, University of Oxford and Wytham Woods Genome Acquisition Lab, Darwin Tree of Life Barcoding Collective, Wellcome Sanger Institute Tree of Life Management, Samples and Laboratory team, Wellcome Sanger Institute Scientific Operations: Sequencing Operations, Wellcome San
pmc-13562948.description: We present a genome assembly from an individual male Trichiura crataegi (Pale Eggar; Arthropoda; Insecta; Lepidoptera; Lasiocampidae). The assembly contains two haplotypes with total lengths of 1 112.64 megabases and 1 115.22 megabases. Most of haplotype 1 (99.87%) is scaffolded into 28 chromosomal pseudomolecules, including the Z sex chromosome. Haplotype 2 was assembled to scaffold level.

pmc-13586560.title: Kindness has a future in health care
pmc-13586560.creator: Victor M. Montori, Dominique Allwood, Leonard L. Berry
pmc-13586560.description: Kindness can seem out of place in contemporary health care systems often shaped by efficiency, industrial logic, and digital surveillance. Yet kindness – understood not as sentiment but as a deliberate practice of kinship expressed in action – is essential to care, the core mission of healthcare.
